description: Expected closure/rule diagnostics list for lib/conformance/fixture-corpus/, produced by pyfars.closure.rule.compose_rules.run and jsfars's composeRules (design spec section 11, conformance vector #4). Diagnostics are compared in this canonical shape (rule, path, slug, target, message), in run order: jsfars's makeDiagnostic already emits exactly this shape; pyfars's richer Diagnostic (severity + a free-form extra dict) is normalized down to it by each language's conformance test, not by production code (see the residual note below).
notes: Rule names are the shared vocabulary both languages must use for every generic closure rule: cycles, broken-links, ambiguous-reference, stubs, orphans, status-consistency, missing-status, missing-proof, wip-theorem, symbols. pyfars.closure.rule.proofs already emitted the latter three as distinct codes; jsfars/src/closure/rules/proofs.mjs was the side that collapsed them into one "proofs" name and has been split to match.

Residual, not exercised by this fixture: pyfars.closure.rule.ambiguous_reference addresses records by path-suffix (extra["target"] is a joined path-component string) while jsfars/src/closure/rules/ambiguous-reference.mjs addresses them by bare slug (target is edge.dst) — the two only coincide when a corpus has no actual path-suffix ambiguity, which this fixture corpus does not exercise.
pyfars.closure.rule.cycles reports slug=target=the self-loop slug for a length-1 cycle and slug=target=null for a multi-node cycle (no single file owns it) — same as jsfars.
